newsitem.title: FRANCE: PARIS BOURSE CLOSES SLIGHTLY LOWER. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PARIS BOURSE CLOSES SLIGHTLY LOWER. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: French shares finished slightly lower on Monday on profit-taking after EU leaders struck a compromise agreement to enforce budget discipline in the single European currency zone and strive to create more jobs.
The blue chip CAC-40 index hit a record high early in the day on anticipation a deal would be reached.
Brokers say the market is now shifting its focus to Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote policy address on June 19.
* CAC-40 index closed down 12.65 points, or 0.45 percent, at 2,795.87
(Corrects from "closed down 2.42 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,795.87")
* CAC-40 Jun futures 2,787 vs 2,786 at Mondays close.
Volume was 6.7 billion francs, relatively modest as many investors held to the sidelines ahead of the Amsterdam summit declaration.

After three sessions of gains and a rise early on Monday to an all time high of 2,825.18 points, the bourse was due for a consolidation, traders said. In addition to the political and monetary developments in Europe,investors are waiting for U.S. consumer price, capacity utilisation and industrial production data on Tuesday.
One broker noted the bourse has become expensive, with a Price-Earnings ratio of 27, surpassed in Europe only by Germany, Switzerland and Hungary.

Eurotunnel shares rose 4.65 percent to 6.75 francs after Shuttle freight service, damaged by fire last year, resumed on schedule on Sunday. Share did not react to report of minority shareholders' call for probe for alleged misuse of corporate funds prior to 1994. * Weakness persists in defence stocks on restructuring concerns. Dassault Aviation closed down 0.84 percent, Thomson-CSF fell 1.2 percent.
* Bertrand Faure rose 6.67 percent to 320 francs on speculation related to the car parts industry's consolidation.
